sections.heading: What is the Sliding Window Pattern?
sections.content: Sliding Window keeps a contiguous range (the window) over an array or string and moves it forward one step at a time. Instead of recomputing the answer for every range from scratch, you update it by adding the new element and removing the old one. This turns O(n * k) or O(n²) solutions into O(n).

sections.heading: When to Use It
items: The problem asks about a contiguous subarray or substring
Keywords: longest, shortest, maximum, minimum, at most K, exactly K, window of size K
You can update the answer cheaply when one element enters or leaves
Input is an array or string (all positives for sum-based shrinking)
You want O(n) time instead of checking every subarray

sections.heading: Sliding Window vs Prefix Sum
items: Sliding window needs a condition that gets better or worse as the window grows (monotonic)
With only positive numbers, a larger window always has a larger sum, so shrinking works
With negative numbers, shrinking does not always reduce the sum, so use Prefix Sum + HashMap
For 'subarray sum equals K' with negatives, do not use sliding window

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
items: Using sliding window on arrays with negative numbers for sum problems
Updating the answer in the wrong place (longest: after loop, shortest: inside loop)
Forgetting to remove a key from the map when its count reaches 0
Off by one: window size is right - left + 1
Using if instead of while when shrinking, so the window stays invalid
Not handling k larger than the array length
Forgetting that exactly K is atMost(K) - atMost(K - 1)

rows.approach: Variable window with counter or set

sections.heading: Why Variable Window is O(n)
sections.content: It looks like a nested loop, but each element enters the window once (right pointer) and leaves at most once (left pointer). That is at most 2n pointer moves in total, so the time is O(n).

sections.heading: Key Takeaways
items: Sliding window is for contiguous subarrays and substrings
Fixed window: add one, remove one, update the answer
Variable window: expand right, shrink left while the condition is broken
Longest: update after shrinking. Shortest: update while valid
Exactly K equals atMost(K) minus atMost(K - 1)
Each element enters and leaves once, so the time is O(n)
